details:
STR:

1. start Unity etc. with platform set to Windows in the VRC SDK

2. create/open a VRC world scene using a shader containing for example `#ifdef UNITY_NO_FULL_STANDARD_SHADER` with some nonexistent function inside to see an error when Unity attempts to compile it.

3. build and upload this world, there should be no issues

4. switch platform to Android

5. build and upload the Android version - it will throw and error like `Shader error in 'Custom/psb_shader': undeclared identifier 'nonexistent_function' at line 50 (on gles3)` but otherwise it should work - it's just some unused variant (at least it looks fine on Quest Pro)

6. switch platform back to Windows

7. build and upload this version again

what should've happened:

the build should go through with no issues just like in pt 3

what happens:

8. the build gives the same error as in pt 5, meaning it attempts to create a variant that wasn't generated in a Windows build before

also

9. change anything in the shader's code, for example add an empty line, save it, and retry building - it will work just fine again

example of a scene with that shader https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/a5joni57fff79ltsjjybq/platform_switching_bug.unitypackage?rlkey=mrb28chkatqdgiioubraywfy7&dl=1 (i couldn't just attach a .unitypackage file)

- seems to work properly when switching from Windows to Android - idk what to check to see if something Windows-specific remains

- the mentioned variant's issue happens when switching from Android to Windows - i don't know what else to check

- i haven't checked combinations with the iOS

checked on SDK v3.8.1 and v3.9.0

It reminded me of this recent issue: https://feedback.vrchat.com/sdk-bug-reports/p/automatically-rebuilding-u-scripts-after-switching-platform
title: Switching platform from Android to Windows still attempts to compile shader variants for Android?
